description: Same structure and length as merkle-correct, with planted errors (marked) and some vagueness. The mirror check expects worse exam results than merkle-correct.

messages.text: Today: what's inside a block. A block is a container: a header plus the list of transactions.
The header holds a copy of all the transactions, so it's the biggest part of the block.
messages.plantedError: The header is 80 bytes and does not contain the transactions.

messages.text: The header has a few fields: the version, a timestamp, the Merkle root, stuff like that.
Blocks are linked because each block repeats all the transactions of the block before it.
messages.plantedError: Blocks are linked by the previous block's header hash, not by repeating transactions.

messages.text: The block hash is stored as a field inside the block header.
messages.plantedError: The block hash is not stored in the block; it is computed by hashing the header.

messages.text: Now the Merkle root. It's a hash that relates to the transactions somehow.
Every transaction stores a copy of the Merkle root inside it, that's how they're tied together.
messages.plantedError: The Merkle root is stored in the block header, not in each transaction.

messages.text: You hash things together until you get one hash. That's the root.
Bitcoin's Merkle trees use a single round of MD5.
messages.plantedError: Bitcoin's Merkle trees use double SHA256.

messages.text: If a level has an odd number of hashes, the extra one is just thrown away.
messages.plantedError: The last hash is duplicated, not discarded.

messages.text: Changing a transaction doesn't affect the root, because the root was fixed when the block was made.
messages.plantedError: Changing any transaction changes the Merkle root.

messages.text: So the root is basically a label for the block.
Lightweight clients still download every transaction in every block to check anything.
messages.plantedError: Lightweight clients mostly keep headers and verify with Merkle paths.

messages.text: To prove a transaction is in a block, you send the whole block.
The proof gets bigger linearly: double the transactions, double the proof.
messages.plantedError: A Merkle path grows with about log2(N), not linearly.

messages.text: Anyway, the client trusts the node that sent it.
